observations.body: Before blessing Israel, Moses recalls the LORD coming from Sinai, shining from Seir and Paran, accompanied by ten thousands of holy ones, with fiery law and gathered tribes.
observations.label: Sinai is remembered with holy ones and fiery law

observations.body: Sinai is remembered with holy ones and fiery law belongs to sinai remembered in the Sinai trail.
observations.label: Where this sits

observations.body: Deuteronomy 33:1–5 supplies later-memory evidence for the event’s developing sequence.
observations.label: Within the Sinai event

observations.body: Later witnesses select and reuse Sinai in their own settings; they remain later readings rather than replacements for the Exodus event.
observations.label: Reading boundary

payload.posture: Read Deuteronomy 33:1–5 as its own source before carrying it into the wider Sinai trail.
payload.tension: Sinai is remembered with holy ones and fiery law belongs to the sinai remembered movement, but its part in the event must remain distinct from the surrounding speech, response, breach, and renewal.
payload.title: Sinai is remembered with holy ones and fiery law
